{{ElectionsMI}}
The '''2026 Michigan gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Michigan]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state secretary of state [[Jocelyn Benson]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. representative [[John James (Michigan politician)|John James]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Democratic incumbent [[Gretchen Whitmer]] is ineligible to seek a third term.

[[Primary elections]] were held on August 4. Benson won the Democratic nomination with 83.2% of the vote over Genesee County sheriff Chris Swanson. Endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]], James won the Republican nomination with 50.1% of the vote over businessman [[Perry Johnson (businessman)|Perry Johnson]].

Republicans have not won a gubernatorial election in Michigan since [[2014 Michigan gubernatorial election|2014]].

{{toclimit|3}}

==Background==
Michigan is a [[Swing state|purple]] state in the heart of the [[Great Lakes]] and [[Rust Belt]] which consistently elected [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] for president since [[1992 United States presidential election in Michigan|1992]] until [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee [[Donald Trump]] narrowly flipped the state in [[2016 United States presidential election in Michigan|2016]]. In [[2020 United States presidential election in Michigan|2020]], Democratic nominee [[Joe Biden]] won Michigan by 2.78%. In the [[2024 United States presidential election in Michigan|2024 presidential election]], Donald Trump won Michigan by 1.42%, which was attributed to [[Joe Biden|President Biden]]'s unpopularity and rightward shifts in working-class and [[Arab Americans|Arab American]] voters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michigan Presidential Election Voting History - 270toWin |url=https://www.270towin.com/states/michigan |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=270toWin.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Shalal |first=Andrea |date=November 10, 2024 |title=Kamala Harris' Michigan loss highlights Democrats' weak spots |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/harris-michigan-loss-highlights-democrats-many-weak-spots-2024-11-10/ |access-date=January 1, 2026 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

Since the [[2018 Michigan elections]], Democrats occupied all statewide offices in Michigan. Since [[2022 Michigan Senate election|2022]], Democrats held a narrow majority in the [[Michigan Senate|State Senate]] while Republicans held a narrow majority in the [[Michigan House of Representatives]] since [[2024 Michigan House of Representatives election|2024]]. According to the [[Morning Consult]], which measures the popularity of governors across the country, Democratic governor [[Gretchen Whitmer]] has a net +26 approval rating in Michigan as of September 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2026 |title=Tracking the Approval Ratings of All 50 U.S. Governors |url=https://pro.morningconsult.com/trackers/governor-approval-ratings |access-date=September 24, 2026 |website=[[Morning Consult]]}}</ref>

In [[2018 Michigan gubernatorial election|2018]], Gretchen Whitmer and her running mate [[Garlin Gilchrist]] won by 9.56%. In [[2022 Michigan gubernatorial election|2022]], Whitmer and Gilchrist won by 10.53%.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leip |first=David |title=2018 Gubernatorial General Election Results - Michigan |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/results/state.php?year=2018&fips=26&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250218051919/https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?year=2018&fips=26&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-date=2025-02-18 |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=uselectionatlas.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Leip |first=David |title=2022 Gubernatorial General Election Results - Michigan |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/results/state.php?year=2022&fips=26&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204065112/https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=26&year=2022&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |archive-date=2024-12-04 |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=uselectionatlas.org}}</ref>

The deadline for candidates to submit petitions to run for governor in the partisan primaries was Tuesday, April 21, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Basso |first1=Dan |last2=Williams |first2=Jalen |date=April 20, 2026 |title=Michigan governor filing deadline just ahead. Here's who's running |url=https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/news/politics/2026/04/20/governor-gretchen-whitmer-candidates-election-2026-deadline/89697669007/ |access-date=April 22, 2026 |website=[[Lansing State Journal]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== General election ==

=== Campaign ===
In September 2026, the [[Libertarian Party of Michigan]] formally disavowed connections and support to Anthony Hudson, their gubernatorial nominee. The party stated that Hudson's campaign was promoting positions that contradicted their purpose as a party, while Hudson responded and said that he was comfortable with their disavowal. Given that this happened after the withdrawal deadline had passed, Hudson's name will still appear listed as the party's nominee on the election ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dailey |first=Katherine |date=September 29, 2026 |title=Michigan Libertarian Party disavows its own gubernatorial nominee |url=https://michiganadvance.com/2026/09/29/michigan-libertarian-party-disavows-its-own-gubernatorial-nominee/ |access-date=September 30, 2026 |website=[[Michigan Advance]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Also in September 2026, it was revealed that Hudson's running mate, Beau Parmenter, had been arrested that month and charged with felony larceny by conversion for an incident from May 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Evans |first1=Jordan Willow |title=Libertarian Candidate for Michigan Lt. Governor Arrested, Charged With Felony Larceny |url=https://independentpoliticalreport.com/2026/09/libertarian-candidate-for-michigan-lt-governor-arrested-charged-with-felony-larceny/ |access-date=October 3, 2026 |work=[[Independent Political Report]] |date=September 18, 2026}}</ref>
